why: The statement asks for the optimal density in every dimension other than 1, 2, 3, 8 and 24, and for its high-dimensional asymptotics. None of the events determines either. Every lower or upper bound on the true density is therefore 'bound': Klartag; Abuya–Gargava–Zhao; the Astra exponent 0.6044 (which fixes the limit of the Cohn–Elkies method but only bounds the density); the dimension-specific records; and the Huawei SDP bounds. The dimension-9 result is lattice-only, while the statement asks about all packings, so it is a variant. The binary-code result is also a variant. Formalisations of results already proved, Viazovska's excluded dimensions and the conditional pair-correlation work all score none. Klartag counts as digested: Inventiones accepted it, and Aubrun's Bourbaki exposition is a digested rewrite. AI roles: Abuya et al. say the model proposed the method and proved the bound, with humans verifying it, so that event is generated. For Astra, the quote only mentions formalisation, but the whole announcement credits the model with producing the result, so I answered generated. Huawei/UCL is the closest call. Its system is Bayesian optimisation with tree search, not a language model, but it produced the SDP structures that give the bounds, and the authors frame it as AI. I answered assisted.
doubts: Astra's ai_basis quote is about formalisation. The generated call rests on OpenAI's overall attribution, as relayed by secondary sources, not on a verbatim primary quote. The Huawei/UCL role depends on whether BO+MCTS search counts as an AI system, and its basis is a paraphrase. For Gargava–Viazovska and Jumagulov, the record does not say whether they actually improve on prior bounds. Klartag's journal acceptance comes from a search-result header only.
